title: MIT OpenCourseWare 15.515 Financial Accounting, Fall 2003 — Session 13: Long-term Debt
use: Dated primary teaching support for face/coupon/market/effective-rate distinctions, discount and premium, issuance/accrual/payment/retirement and book-versus-market value. Original chapter examples are not source exercises.
verification: Retrieved and read actual seven-page lecture PDF, especially terminology, discount/premium and statement-presentation slides. The source's no-fee effective-rate/issue-market-rate simplification is not extended to the chapter's fee-adjusted borrower yield. Old classification notes are not presented as a full current reporting rule.

title: AASB 9 Financial Instruments — December 2022 compiled version
use: Scoped amortized-cost liability, directly attributable transaction-cost and effective-interest definitions; full extinguishment versus consideration paid. Fees for separate services are distinguished from integral financing fees.
verification: Actual official archived Australian text inspected: version metadata (periods beginning 1 January 2023 to before 1 January 2026), 5.1.1, Appendix A effective-interest definition, B5.4.1–B5.4.4 and B5.4.8, and 3.3.1/3.3.3. Used for the stated method and historical scope, not to assert all 2026 transactions satisfy current classification/measurement rules. No expected-credit-loss adjustment imported into this borrower schedule.

title: IFRS Foundation — Investor Update, September 2020: lessee accounting reminder
use: Primary explanation of right-of-use asset, present-value lease liability, depreciation and interest as separate amounts. Supports the chapter's bounded lessee model, not a full lease-identification or modification treatment.
verification: Actual September2020 investor article inspected, especially 'Reminder—How lessees apply IFRS16'. Adjacent pandemic-concession discussion was read but is not applied to the synthetic fixed-payment case. Public IFRS16 overview also inspected for context. Attempted 2021 full IFRS16 PDF redirected to subscription page; full standard was not inspected or claimed.

title: FASB In Focus — Accounting Standards Update 2016-02, Leases (Topic 842), revised 3 June 2020
use: Dated comparison: both US finance and operating leases recognize right-of-use assets/liabilities under the described model, while income/cash presentation differs; operating leases retain a single straight-line expense pattern.
verification: Actual four-page FASB publication inspected, especially pages2–3 and the page3 comparison table. Its historical 'current GAAP' language describes the transition context, not today's off-balance-sheet rule. Publication is a staff educational summary with its stated status limitation; the full current Codification and subsequent amendments were not inspected. No blanket current IFRS/US-GAAP equivalence claimed.

title: IASB — October 2022 announcement: long-term debt with covenants
use: Dated distinction between reporting-date debt classification and disclosures about covenants to be complied with after that date; announced effective date 1 January 2024.
verification: Actual announcement body inspected, including 12-month settlement rights, subsequent-compliance covenant scope, disclosure purpose and effective date. The chapter's leverage covenant, waiver/acceleration alternatives and liquidity thresholds are original contract assumptions, not universal legal consequences. Full amended IAS1 text not claimed as inspected.
